acme_integration: hey @support — our indexer started rejecting a big chunk of vectors after last night's model swap. seeing repeated errors in the backfill worker: `dim mismatch: expected 2048 got 512`. backfill is retrying in a tight loop and our bill spiked. can someone triage?

support_jana: sorry about that — can you paste a sample request/response and the model id you were using? any recent deploy or config change?

acme_integration: here's the call that used to work, and a failing response from the indexer:```
POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/embeddings
Body: {"model": "rw-embed-2048", "input": "some text"}
Response (old): {"embedding": [0.12, ...] /* length: 2048 */}
Response (now): {"embedding": [0.03, ...] /* length: 512 */}
Indexer error (log): {"error": "invalid_vector_length", "expected": 2048, "got": 512, "ids": ["doc-123", "doc-124"]}```

acme_integration: model was auto-updated at 2026-01-14T02:12:08Z — new model id: `rw-embed-lite-v2-small`. we didn't pin in our infra; backfill started last night and is still running.

ingest_oncall: grabbing indexer logs — confirmed: lots of rejects: `Rejecting 512-dim vector for index 'customer_xyz' (expected 2048)`. backfill consumer marks failed task as retryable and requeues. result: failed docs get retried repeatedly, causing duplicate attempts and increased request counts to embeddings endpoint.

indexer-bot: [2026-01-14T03:21:11Z] WARN backfill-consumer: 493/1200 vectors rejected (invalid_vector_length). Requeue rate: 1.8/s. DB inserts rolled back for failed items.

support_jana: two separate problems: (1) model produced smaller embeddings (512) without a pinned model, (2) backfill logic requeues failed docs instead of moving them to a dead-letter queue, causing re-ingest/recharge. we'll need engineering oncall for pipeline changes and billing review. @eng_eli can you take?

eng_eli: on it. Quick mitigation checklist: 1) stop the active backfill job to prevent further retries and cost; 2) temporarily allow the index to accept 512-dim vectors (if semantically ok) OR pad/upsample embeddings to 2048; 3) add dedupe/dead-letter to backfill so we don't re-run same failing doc; 4) figure out why model swap wasn't pinned.

eng_eli: to stop backfill (if you're running the k8s job):```
kubectl -n ingest scale job/backfill-customer-xyz --replicas=0
# or via internal admin API (prod):
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.internal/api/backfills/stop -d '{"id":"bf-9876"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

acme_integration: stopped the job, thanks. we also want to avoid data loss — we need guidance on fixing existing failed docs.

ingest_oncall: two repair options: A) re-run embeddings for all docs with pinned 2048 model (expensive), B) re-ingest current 512 vectors and update index schema to store dimension metadata + modify downstream ranking to handle mixed dims (safer short-term). if you need vector lengths uniform for ANN engine, you can pad with zeros: `pad_vector(v, target_len=2048)` — not ideal but fast.

eng_eli: engineering note: padding example in python (quick hack):```
def pad_to_2048(vec):
    if len(vec) == 2048: return vec
    return vec + [0.0] * (2048 - len(vec))

# load failing docs, apply pad_to_2048, reindex```

billing_sara: flagged a billing ticket BILL-2026-453 for review, please include estimate of extra token/embedding calls. we'll validate credits once we have numbers.

support_jana: follow-ups / action items: • acme_integration stopped backfill (confirmed) • eng_eli to open runtime incident to prevent unpinned model swaps for embedding endpoints • ingest_oncall to add backfill DLQ + dedupe (short-term patch) • eng_eli + acme to decide on repair strategy (pad vs re-embed) • billing_sara to review credits (BILL-2026-453)

eng_eli: immediate plan: i'll push a guard that blocks model auto-promotions for any `embed-*` family unless pin=true in project config. medium-term: add dimension-mismatch validator in indexer to detect model changes and fail fast (before backfill).

acme_integration: thanks all — we'll coordinate on whether to re-embed (clean) vs pad (faster). please keep us posted on credits, and any ETA on the runtime guard.

support_jana: closing the Slack thread — we'll keep the ticket open in support. tagging docs: we should add a note to the onboarding guide about pinning embedding model versions and a backfill-operator playbook. :memo:
